topic: Sharp exponent thresholds for Dietz, Flowers and Lockard's self-conjugate conjugate m-ary partition questions
title: Sharp thresholds for Dietz, Flowers and Lockard's self-conjugate partition questions: extending Flowers and Lockard's construction

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Using Munagi's residue-class criterion (2008, Theorem 3.1) and extending Flowers and Lockard's construction (2021, Lemma 4.2, p. 467), we answer Questions 5.12–5.14 of Dietz, Flowers and Lockard's A study of m-ary partitions whose conjugates are q-ary (2026, §5, p. 404) in their self-conjugate setting: among conjugate m-ary partitions, the first odd exponent admitting a self-conjugate partition for even m is m+1, the first exponent admitting a non-square self-conjugate partition for any m is m+1, and odd exponents are impossible for odd m. A row-multiplicity identity gives N ≡ H+W−1 modulo (m−1)(q−1) for conjugate (m,q)-ary partitions. For partitions of m^r it yields a positive exponent defect divisible by m−1 whenever the diagram is not rectangular. This proves the exact nonrectangular threshold and, with the credited constructions, classifies all exponents admitting a non-square self-conjugate partition.
summary: A nonrectangular CMP of m^r exists exactly for r ≥ m+1. Non-square self-conjugate examples exist exactly for even r ≥ m+1 when m is odd, odd r ≥ m+1 when m is even, or even r ≥ 2m when m is even. A word-counting consequence gives density zero if m^(-1/2)+q^(-1/2)<1, and also for (m,q)=(4,4). The written proofs use a product-modulus identity and credited constructions.
